hedges.reason: A GPT-6 launch before mid-2026 is the clearest way for OpenAI to take the top spot on LMArena by June 30. A new flagship generation usually debuts at #1 on Arena, and Google (Gemini 3.x) is the default leader otherwise. This contract pays in the early-GPT-6 worlds where my C2 NO and C3 NO legs lose.

Competitor major-version launches are the demand side of the hedge thesis. In a fast frontier race where OpenAI speeds its flagship schedule, Anthropic shipping Claude 5 early (the later, April 30 rung) is the matching competitor move. The link is weak and the ladder only runs to April, so it mostly covers the C1 failure world.

This is the supply side of the hedge thesis. An early GPT-6 needs abundant frontier compute and an AI-capex boom, and those are the worlds where Nvidia stays the largest company by June 30. It is a weak, partly default-state hedge, and the only listed instrument tied to AI capex.

claims.reason: If OpenAI makes GPT-6 public by June 30, then on June 30 OpenAI has a brand-new major-generation flagship. OpenAI names a model 'GPT-6' only for a clear capability step over GPT-5.x, and a fresh flagship of that kind usually sits at or near #1 on LMArena text in the weeks after release. So a GPT-6-by-June world is one where OpenAI holds the top Arena spot on June 30.
